I found one that is actually worth interrupting you for:

**NETGEAR Nighthawk M6 Pro 5G Hotspot — $250 — McKinney, TX — Facebook Marketplace.** The listing is marked **used / like new** and specifically says **“Paid Off – AT&T.”** Facebook’s public index surfaced it within the last two days.

The one caveat: **paid off does not necessarily mean already carrier-unlocked.** If you’re okay using AT&T prepaid, that may not matter; otherwise I’d ask the seller whether the unlock has already been completed before driving to McKinney.

urlOpen the McKinney Marketplace search for this M6 Pro listinghttps://www.facebook.com/marketplace/mckinney/search/?query=NETGEAR%20Nighthawk%20M6%20Pro%205G%20Hotspot%20Paid%20Off

At **$250** it’s not the cheapest M6 Pro on earth, but given the “need it before the trip” constraint, this is the first local one I’ve found that clears the **good hardware / outright ownership / realistic pickup** bar.
Can't do it. McKinney is about four hours in the opposite direction, and $250 is way, way, way, way beyond budget.

Understood. McKinney and the $200+ tier are out. I’m tightening this to **Fort Worth and the west/southwest DFW corridor—especially anything naturally on the way toward New Mexico—and genuinely cheap enough to be useful rather than merely “a good deal.”**
Yeah dude, unfortunately you have to actually remember Dallas-Fort Worth geographically is not like anywhere else in North America.

Exactly. “DFW” is a **market label**, not a useful pickup radius. McKinney/Frisco/Plano can be effectively another fucking city when you’re starting in Fort Worth—especially the night before a westbound trip.

I’m treating this as **drive-time geography from Fort Worth**, not “within X miles of DFW”: Fort Worth proper first; then west/southwest/northwest places like White Settlement, Benbrook, Aledo, Weatherford, Saginaw/Azle, and only Arlington/Mid-Cities if the deal is genuinely worth the detour. **Dallas proper, Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Aubrey, etc. do not count as local for this search.**

Yep. I’ve corrected the search logic accordingly.

The watch now treats **Fort Worth as the origin point**, not “DFW” as one giant blob, and it will check hourly through Thursday night. It won’t bother you with Plano/Frisco/McKinney/Aubrey nonsense or $200–$250 “deals.”

I’m filtering for **cheap enough to actually matter + obtainable without screwing up your westbound trip + hardware worth trusting on the road**. If nothing clears all three bars, you won’t hear from it.
All right. Well, I'm assuming while you are monitoring that, you're not actively working as in you are not. So if that's the case, we've got some stuff we can continue with.

Correct. The monitoring task is scheduled separately; I’m not “occupied” by it between checks.

We can keep working on anything else right now, and if that watch finds something genuinely worth acting on, it can surface it independently.

Okay, there's a whole section in there for using tiny and small models in Oh My Pi. We've been talking about using Cactus Compute to help offset some of the computational burden of just constant tool calls. I think we need to look at that real fast and just go ahead and get it done and implemented so that it's running. Otherwise we're going to keep stomping on our feet about it.

Yeah. This is exactly the kind of thing worth fixing now instead of paying the tool-call tax all night. I’m going to trace the existing Oh My Pi small-model path, identify where Cactus fits as a local/offload execution layer, and then wire the smallest viable implementation into the current stack rather than designing another abstraction we never turn on.

I found the architectural intent, and there’s an important distinction in it: **Cactus/Needle was supposed to be the reflex/micro-router—cheap tool selection, schema extraction, salience gating—not part of identity or the durable state layer.** That means we can turn it on without violating the compute/model boundary or binding Dottie/GrizOS to a particular model provider. 

I’m tracing the live Oh My Pi/OpenRig repository now so I can implement that exact boundary and test it in-place rather than treating the old handoff as executable truth.

You’re right to check. The last remote probe did **not** return before this turn interrupted it, so I do **not** have the right to sit here and imply implementation is progressing invisibly.

I’m going back onto the Mac **now**, locating the live Oh My Pi/OpenRig tree, and I’m not going to give you another status paragraph until I have either (a) the actual code path in hand or (b) a concrete blocker.

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

os.environ.setdefault("NEEDLE_TELEMETRY", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("DO_NOT_TRACK", "1")

import needle

HOST = os.environ.get("CACTUS_REFLEX_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
PORT = int(os.environ.get("CACTUS_REFLEX_PORT", "8765"))
ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("CACTUS_REFLEX_ROOT", Path.home() / ".omp/agent/cactus-reflex"))
CACHE = ROOT / "cache"
CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

_lock = threading.RLock()
_agents: dict[str, needle.Needle] = {}


def _tool_fingerprint(tools: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    raw = json.dumps(tools, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()[:20]


def _agent_for(tools: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> needle.Needle:
    key = _tool_fingerprint(tools)
    with _lock:
        agent = _agents.get(key)
        if agent is not None:
            return agent

        index_path = str(CACHE / f"tools-{key}.idx")
        agent = needle.Needle(
            tools=tools,
            tool_index_path=index_path,
            stateless=True,
        )
        _agents.clear()
        _agents[key] = agent
        return agent


def route(prompt: str, tools: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not prompt.strip() or not tools:
        return {"ok": True, "names": [], "confidence": 0.0, "raw": None}

    result = _agent_for(tools).complete(prompt, max_new_tokens=256)
    calls = result.get("function_calls") or []
    names: list[str] = []
    for call in calls:
        if not isinstance(call, dict):
            continue
        name = call.get("name")
        if isinstance(name, str) and name not in names:
            names.append(name)

    confidence = result.get("confidence", 0.0)
    try:
        confidence = float(confidence)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        confidence = 0.0

    return {
        "ok": True,
        "names": names,
        "confidence": confidence,
        "type": result.get("type"),
        "success": bool(result.get("success", True)),
        "suppressed_calls": result.get("suppressed_calls") or [],
    }


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "GMRI-CactusReflex/1.0"

    def log_message(self, fmt: str, *args: Any) -> None:
        return

    def _json(self, code: int, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        if self.path == "/health":
            self._json(200, {"ok": True, "service": "cactus-reflex", "agents": len(_agents)})
            return
        self._json(404, {"ok": False, "error": "not_found"})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/route":
            self._json(404, {"ok": False, "error": "not_found"})
            return

        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
            payload = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
            prompt = payload.get("prompt", "")
            tools = payload.get("tools", [])
            if not isinstance(prompt, str) or not isinstance(tools, list):
                raise ValueError("prompt must be a string and tools must be a list")
            self._json(200, route(prompt, tools))
        except Exception as exc:
            self._json(500, {"ok": False, "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ThreadingHTTPServer((HOST, PORT), Handler).serve_forever()
","mode":"rewrite"}}

One concrete measurement from the live OMP configuration: a GitHub-only request reduces the available tool descriptions from **23,639 to 11,118 characters**, a 53% reduction. That is not yet a measured reduction in tokens, latency, or total compute cost.

The larger issue remains Cactus itself: cold inference is too slow. I'm testing whether keeping its model loaded can eliminate that overhead without risking OMP stability.

The native benchmark has identified the bottleneck: with Needle kept in one process, five routing requests completed in **27–34 milliseconds each**, using approximately 121 MB of peak process memory.

That changes the repair: keep Needle resident in a crash-isolated worker instead of starting Python and loading its dependencies on every tool decision.

The resident-worker stress test has now completed **20 of 20 limited routing checks**, with a warm median of **26.7 ms** and no process crashes. That's strong evidence the repeated process startup—not Needle's actual routing speed—was causing the earlier delay.

I'm moving from the standalone benchmark to the supervised service integration. Until that's connected to OMP, those benchmark results do not count as deployment completion.

The replacement service has now passed its first live HTTP routing request: **97 ms**, with Needle selecting GitHub correctly. The worker was already running, and OMP itself remained separate from the native process.

I'm finishing the production connection and its failure-handling checks now.

The production launch service has now restarted with the resident-worker implementation. Its metrics confirm the new worker is alive. The earlier cold-start-per-request design is no longer what the production service is running.

The OMP extension has also been rebuilt to consult Needle on eligible ambiguous requests, with conservative fallbacks when confidence is insufficient.

The production stress test exposed another issue: although the resident worker is fast in isolation, live requests on the Mac took roughly **0.5–1.6 seconds**, and two oversized cases timed out.

I'm checking system contention and the worker's recovery behavior rather than accepting the isolated benchmark as representative. The extension's fail-open behavior is important here: a delayed or failed model decision must not remove necessary tools.

That scheduling test found the performance problem.

Changing the launch service from **Background** to **Standard** reduced the live Needle requests to **25–30 ms after warmup**, with the first request at 153 ms. The oversized request now fails open in 2 ms rather than tying up the worker.

This is measured through the production HTTP service, not just a standalone Python benchmark.

Crash recovery is now verified too. I deliberately terminated the native Needle worker, then ran the production routing checks again.

The supervising service stayed up, started a replacement worker, and successfully handled the subsequent requests. Its metrics show **two worker starts, 11 successful inference requests, zero native-response failures, and one live replacement worker**. The oversized requests were rejected safely before inference.

The extension has also passed the three important live OMP paths: ordinary startup loads it automatically; a single-tool request filters **25 tools to 9 in about 5 ms**; and a compound GitHub-plus-web request preserves all 25 tools.

An ambiguous request actually reached Needle, but its confidence was low, so OMP correctly retained the full tool set instead of guessing. I'm now checking provider-reported usage rather than equating shorter tool descriptions with actual savings.

We now have a provider-reported savings measurement from matched OMP prompts:

| Metric | Full tools | Filtered tools |
|---|---:|---:|
| Active tools | 25 | 9 |
| Prompt tokens, including cached reads | 15,078 | 12,686 |
| Reported request cost | $0.002287 | $0.001428 |

That's **2,392 fewer prompt tokens, or approximately 15.9%**, in this comparison.

The reported cost was also lower, but the two runs had different cache usage, so I will not attribute that entire cost difference to routing. 

The normal, unmodified OMP startup also exposed a separate blocker: its Laya Judge MCP plugin was configured to launch a Windows `.cmd` file on macOS.

I corrected the launcher to use the installed Python environment and bridge. A subsequent normal OMP session completed successfully, and its log shows the Laya Judge MCP commands being registered.

    {"name": "web_search", "description": "Search current web documentation", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}},
    {"name": "generate_image", "description": "Generate image artwork", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}},
]


def get(path):
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + path, timeout=4))


def post(prompt, tools=TOOLS):
    body = json.dumps({"prompt": prompt, "tools": tools}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/route", data=body, headers={"content-type": "application/json"})
    start = time.perf_counter()
    result = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=4))
    return result, round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)

    ("Generate image artwork of a bear", "generate_image"),

assert long_prompt.get("ok") is False and duration < 100, (long_prompt, duration)
print("LONG_PROMPT_REJECTED", duration, flush=True)

body = b"x" * 32769

    urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(BASE+"/route", data=body), timeout=4)
    raise AssertionError("oversized request accepted")
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
    assert e.code == 413, e.code
print("BODY_LIMIT_413", flush=True)

metrics = get("/metrics")
assert metrics["worker_alive"] and metrics["success"] >= 25, metrics
print("METRICS", json.dumps(metrics), flush=True)
print("ACCEPTANCE_PASS", flush=True)

## Scope
A localhost-only, crash-isolated tiny-model *tool-name selector* for Oh My Pi.
This layer **does not execute tools**, store durable memories, or serve as an OMP chat model.
No claim is made that Dottie Hill, GrizzOS, OpenRig, God's Eye View, or any other
GMRI deliverable is certified by these tests.

## Installed locations
- OMP CLI: `/Users/rbhanson/.bun/bin/omp` (18.8.0 at deployment)
- OMP auto-loaded extension: `~/.omp/agent/extensions/cactus-reflex.js`
- Editable source and tests: `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/`
- Python venv: `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/venv/`
- Dependency lock: `requirements.lock.txt` (includes cactus-needle==3.1.2)
- LaunchAgent: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.grizzlymedicine.omp-cactus-reflex.plist`
- TCP endpoint: `127.0.0.1:8765` (not internet exposed)

## Behavior and limitations
- Obvious single-tool request: grounded lexical fast path, always-on core tools remain available.
- Ambiguous 2-3 candidate request: resident Cactus Needle can advise tool selection.
- Needle output must report success, one selected known tool, grounded to request,
  and confidence >=0.75 to narrow availability.
- Multi-step, negated, long (>1600-character), low-confidence, errored,
  busy, or unreachable routing: fail open (do not suppress enabled tools).
- The original enabled-tool state is restored at session shutdown, including
  user changes to tool permissions made after a previous routing decision.
- OMP extension request deadline: 900 ms. HTTP service maximum body: 32,768 bytes.
  Inference worker timeout: 2.5 seconds. Two requests admitted concurrently;
  overload returns HTTP 503 promptly. Native crashes do not bring down OMP.
- The service is for local routing. Other MCP plugin compatibility must be
  validated independently.

## Local verification
```sh
cd /Users/rbhanson/.omp/agent
bun test cactus-reflex/core.test.ts cactus-reflex/extension.test.ts
cd cactus-reflex
./venv/bin/python -m py_compile router.py needle_worker.py
./venv/bin/python http_acceptance.py
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8765/health
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8765/metrics
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/org.grizzlymedicine.omp-cactus-reflex
```

## Field diagnostics
- In an interactive OMP session, run `/cactus-reflex` for the last route.
- OMP logs: `~/.omp/logs/omp.YYYY-MM-DD.PID.log`.
- Service logs: `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/logs/`.
- Health means *service available*, not proof that every route is correct.
- `source=lexical` and `source=needle` are distinct. Do not interpret
  lexical source as a Needle confidence score.

## Rollback without deleting project data
Move `~/.omp/agent/extensions/cactus-reflex.js` out of the OMP extensions
directory (for example to the source directory) and restart the OMP session.
Optional: unload the LaunchAgent using launchctl bootout, but the extension
already fails open if the service cannot be reached.
Do not delete the venv, model caches, or original OMP configuration to roll back.

## Independent plugin compatibility
The installed `omp-laya-judge` package originally referenced a Windows
`laya-judge.cmd` in its `.mcp.json` on this macOS host. Its launcher was
changed to the plugin's own Python `.venv/bin/python` plus `server/bridge.py`.
A future package update could overwrite that vendor configuration.

## Disk safety
Homebrew cached download cleanup was restricted to regular files older than
14 days; the prior list is `old-homebrew-cache-audit.txt`.
The cached OMP installer, installed apps, user projects, and model weights were
not deleted. Monitor free disk before deployment or downloads.

## 3. What stopped us from calling it production-ready?

This is the important discovery from the final tests.

Needle initially produced mostly low-confidence answers when given OMP's long tool descriptions. I experimented with shorter, purpose-built descriptions.

That raised confidence substantially, but **some high-confidence answers were wrong**.

For example, when asked to generate a GitHub image icon, Needle selected the GitHub tool instead of image generation, with approximately 85% reported confidence.

That means confidence alone is not sufficient to decide whether a tool can safely be hidden.

**Those shorter descriptions were experimental and have not been deployed into the active OMP extension.** The production extension still uses its original descriptions and conservative fallback behavior.

There's also the savings question. The safer configuration preserves 18 of 28 tools on a straightforward GitHub request. One matched comparison showed only about 0.8% fewer input tokens. That's a measured improvement, but not enough to demonstrate meaningful overall computational savings.

    with _lock: _stats["fail_open"] += 1
    return {"ok":False,"success":False,"names":[],"error":reason,"model":MODEL}


def route(prompt: str, tools: list[dict]) -> dict:
    with _lock: _stats["requests"] += 1
    if not prompt or len(prompt) > MAX_PROMPT or MULTISTEP.search(prompt):
        return _fail("complex or oversized prompt: preserve all tools")
    if not isinstance(tools,list) or len(tools) not in (2,3):
        return _fail("routing requires 2 or 3 candidates")
    names = [tool.get("name") for tool in tools if isinstance(tool,dict)]
    if len(names) != len(tools) or not all(isinstance(n,str) and n for n in names) or len(set(names)) != len(names):
        return _fail("invalid candidate names")
    target = expected_action(prompt)
    if target is None or target not in names:
        return _fail("ambiguous action: preserve all tools")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([prompt,names],sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    with _lock:
        cached = _cache.get(digest)
        if cached and cached[0] > time.monotonic():
            _cache.move_to_end(digest)
            _stats["cache_hits"] += 1
            return {**cached[1], "cached":True}
    if not _admission.acquire(blocking=False):
        with _lock: _stats["busy"] += 1
        return _fail("router busy")
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        available = "; ".join(f"{n}: {TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS.get(n, str(t.get('description',''))[:100])}" for n,t in zip(names,tools))
        task = f"Tools: {available}; none: no applicable tool.\nTask: {prompt}\n{MODEL_HELP}"
        payload = {
            "model":MODEL,
            "messages":[{"role":"user","content":task}],
            "stream":False,
            "think":False,
            "keep_alive":"30m",
            "options":{"temperature":0,"num_predict":18,"num_ctx":512,"num_thread":4},
        }
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            OLLAMA+"/api/chat",data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
            headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=TIMEOUT) as res:
            answer=json.load(res)
        response = str(answer.get("message",{}).get("content","")).strip().strip('"').strip()
        if response != target:
            with _lock: _stats["mismatches"] += 1
            return _fail("model and independent action guard disagree")
        duration = round((time.monotonic()-start)*1000,1)
        result = {"ok":True,"success":True,"names":[response],
                  "validated":True,"model":MODEL,"latency_ms":duration}
        with _lock:
            _stats["accepted"] += 1
            _times.append(duration)
            _cache[digest] = (time.monotonic()+CACHE_TTL,result)
            _cache.move_to_end(digest)
            while len(_cache)>CACHE_SIZE: _cache.popitem(last=False)
        return result
    except Exception as exc:
        with _lock:
            if isinstance(exc,TimeoutError): _stats["timeouts"] += 1
            else: _stats["upstream_errors"] += 1
        return _fail("upstream inference unavailable: "+type(exc).__name__)
    finally:
        _admission.release()


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "GMRI-GemmaRouter/1.0"
    def log_message(self,*args): return
    def send_json(self,status,payload):
        b=json.dumps(payload,separators=(",",":")).encode()
        try:
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type","application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Length",str(len(b)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b)
        except (BrokenPipeError,ConnectionResetError): pass
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path=="/health":
            try:
                with urllib.request.urlopen(OLLAMA+"/api/version",timeout=0.9) as r:
                    upstream=json.load(r).get("version","unknown")
                self.send_json(200,{"ok":True,"service":"gemma-router","backend":"proxmox-ct106","upstream_version":upstream})
            except Exception:
                self.send_json(503,{"ok":False,"service":"gemma-router","error":"inference host unreachable"})
        elif self.path=="/metrics":
            self.send_json(200,_metrics())
        else:self.send_json(404,{"ok":False,"error":"not_found"})
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path!="/route": return self.send_json(404,{"ok":False,"error":"not_found"})
        try:
            size=int(self.headers.get("Content-Length","0"))
            if size<=0 or size>MAX_BODY: return self.send_json(413,{"ok":False,"error":"body too large"})
            self.connection.settimeout(3.0)
            payload=json.loads(self.rfile.read(size))
            if not isinstance(payload,dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("prompt"),str) or not isinstance(payload.get("tools"),list):
                return self.send_json(400,{"ok":False,"error":"invalid payload"})
            self.send_json(200,route(payload["prompt"],payload["tools"]))
        except Exception:
            self.send_json(400,{"ok":False,"error":"malformed request"})


if __name__=="__main__":
    ThreadingHTTPServer((HOST,PORT),Handler).serve_forever()

I'm staging a guarded router now: straightforward requests stay on the fast path, Gemma handles eligible ambiguous choices, and uncertain or slow results preserve all tools.

**Built and deployed October 8, 2026 (Central time).**
This file is the current authoritative handover for the OMP micro-routing component.
The older README.md contains historic, superseded Cactus Needle prototype notes.

## Architecture and deployed locations
- OMP runs on the GMRI MacBook Air M2 (8 GB RAM); no Gemma weights are stored on it.
- Gemma runs on Proxmox LXC **CT 106**, hostname `ollama-engine`, 24 GiB RAM
  allocation, backed by `local-hdd`; model `gemma4:e2b` (Ollama ID b37049369adf).
- Proxmox node: `100.98.1.114` via private NetBird network. CT 106 internal IP:
  `192.168.4.106`; native Ollama port `11434`.
- Mac LaunchAgent `org.grizzlymedicine.gemma-routing-tunnel` holds an SSH local
  port-forward: `127.0.0.1:11435` -> `192.168.4.106:11434` via Proxmox host.
  SSH is encrypted, loopback bind only, and auto-reconnects when SSH or NetBird returns.
- Mac LaunchAgent `org.grizzlymedicine.omp-gemma-reflex` runs lightweight Python
  `gemma_router.py`, listening on `127.0.0.1:8765`. Its Python venv resides in
  `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/venv/`, retained because it already existed.
  **This service does not import or run Cactus Needle.**
- OMP autoload extension: `~/.omp/agent/extensions/gemma-reflex.js`.
  Editable TypeScript: `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/gemma-reflex.ts`.
  Shared safety logic: `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/core.ts`.
  Interactive OMP status command: `/gemma-reflex`.
- Previous Cactus extension and server prototype retained under
  `~/.omp/agent/cactus-reflex/archive/` for rollback, not loaded automatically.
  Old `org.grizzlymedicine.omp-cactus-reflex` launch job was booted out.

## Behavior
- Clearly grounded single-tool requests: near-zero-cost lexical fast path.
- Only ambiguous 2-3 candidate, single-action requests consult remote Gemma.
- Gemma outputs one tool name (temperature 0, at most 18 output tokens).
- A separate deterministic action guard must agree with Gemma; disagreement,
  unknown tool, no applicable action, multi-step wording, oversized request,
  transport failure, request overload, inference timeout, or low confidence
  **fails open**, preserving all session-enabled tools.
- Core OMP navigation, execution, async and memory tools remain available.
- Changed session permissions are retained; disabling a tool is not silently undone.
- Model acceptance is binary validated=true; **no calibrated confidence is claimed**.
- Model stays warm with Ollama `keep_alive=-1`; Ollama CT 106 is configured to
  start with the container on boot.
- Maximum synchronous routing decision budget at the extension: 3900 ms.
  Inference gateway timeout: 3700 ms. Overload returns immediately without
  dropping ordinary OMP tools. HTTP listen backlog raised to 128.

## Verification conducted
- OMP ordinary startup (without manually adding extensions) loaded gemma-reflex.
- Real end-to-end: "Find web documentation about GitHub" led to a
  `gemma-reflex route` log with `source:gemma`, filtered 18 of 28 eligible
  tools, then the model called the real `web_search` tool and returned results.
- `gemma_router_acceptance.py`: 11/11 production cases passed, including
  GitHub versus image generation, repository security scanning, web documents,
  explicit multi-step fail-open, and no-tool requests. Latest warm median
  routing latency was about 0.89 seconds, p95 about 1.16 seconds on that run.
  Latency can vary with other Proxmox workloads.
- `core.test.ts` + `gemma-reflex.test.ts`: 20 passing automated tests.
- The NetBird-over-SSH tunnel was deliberately terminated and the LaunchAgent
  reconnected to Ollama without manual intervention.
- OMP with an intentionally unreachable router URL logged fail-open with 28/28
  tools, then completed a model response.
- 30 concurrent request load test: 1 accepted and 29 returned immediate
  fail-open "router busy" (zero unexpected failures). That is deliberate
  load shedding on a 4-core CPU, not proof of concurrent inference capacity.
- CT106 model `ollama ps` reported Gemma active on CPU with `UNTIL Forever`.
- Confirmed Proxmox CT106 installed model locally; Mac only hosts router/client.
- PVE root partition was originally 100% full; official apt and journal
  cleanup plus npm cache cleaning restored about 802 MiB of free space.
  **This remains a host capacity risk**, although model weights are on HDD-backed
  CT106 filesystem with separate storage. Mac free disk remains tight.

## Failure behavior and rollback
- If the Mac is offline or NetBird drops while traveling, Gemma routing is
  unavailable; OMP retains all permitted tools and can still use independently
  configured providers if the Mac has its own working internet connection.
- If routing adds unacceptable latency, move
  `~/.omp/agent/extensions/gemma-reflex.js` out of the extension directory,
  then start a fresh OMP session. The gateway and Gemma model can remain in
  place; OMP will run without this routing integration.
- To stop the gateway: `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.grizzlymedicine.omp-gemma-reflex.plist`.
- To stop the tunnel separately: `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.grizzlymedicine.gemma-routing-tunnel.plist`.
- Restoring the old Needle extension requires a deliberate separate decision
  and testing; do not automatically reactivate it.
- Keep the Proxmox HDD-backed model directory and existing Qwen 27B installation
  intact. Do not clear user files or caches that may contain model weights.

## Scope boundary
This release covers Oh My Pi's Gemma tool micro-router only. It is **not** a
production acceptance sign-off for Dottie Hill, GrizzOS, OpenRig, God's Eye
View, or other GMRI beta features. No extensive multi-day uptime soak has
been performed. Per-request fail-open is essential for field use.
